newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady on boosted supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady on boosted supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates steadied on Tuesday on slightly higher supply after a severe lack of kuna funds, dealers said.
"It was easier today. Demand was not overwhelming, and supply was stronger, despite repayment of repo funds," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
The central bank drained some 116 million kuna ($19.3 million) it had granted the banking sector last Friday.
Fresh borrowings fetched 15.5 million kuna against some 20 million on offer. Call money loans, once again steady at 10.5 percent after Monday's rise, accounted for 13.5 million.
The rest were two smaller term loans at 16 and 14 percent.
Monday's overnight trade totalled 10.5 million kuna, mostly sought by one bank for mandatory reserves. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 6.006 Croatian Kuna)
